notes.summary:
MS Office gives 4 to 6 questions in the Tier 2 computer section. In past papers most questions are about Word features and shortcuts, then Excel functions, cell references and sheet limits, then PowerPoint views and slide-show keys.

All shortcuts here are the standard Windows ones for Microsoft 365 and Office 2016 to 2021. Learn them in small families rather than one by one.

concepts.title: Shortcuts that work in all Office programs
concepts.body:
These standard Windows keys work the same way in Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Learn them first; they are asked most often.

KeysWhat it does
Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+VCopy, cut, paste
Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+YUndo, redo (or repeat the last action)
Ctrl+ASelect all
Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+UBold, italic, underline
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+PNew file, open, save, print
F12Save As
Ctrl+W or Ctrl+F4Close the current document (the program stays open)
Alt+F4Close the program window
Ctrl+F, Ctrl+HFind, replace
Ctrl+KInsert a hyperlink for the selected text
F1Help
F7Spelling and grammar check
Ctrl+F1Show or hide the ribbon
Ctrl+Shift+C, Ctrl+Shift+VCopy formatting, paste formatting (Word and PowerPoint)

Mini example: to put a heading in the middle of the line, select it and press Ctrl+E.

concepts.title: Word features and where they live
concepts.body:
The ribbon tabs in Word are File, Home, Insert, Draw, Design, Layout, References, Mailings, Review, View and Help.

TabMain features
HomeFont, paragraph alignment, bullets and numbering, styles, Format Painter, shading, borders, Find and Replace
InsertCover page, blank page, page break, table, pictures, shapes, SmartArt, chart, hyperlink, header, footer, page number, text box, WordArt, drop cap, symbol, equation
DesignThemes, watermark, page colour, page borders
LayoutMargins, orientation (portrait or landscape), size, columns, breaks, line numbers, hyphenation, indent and spacing
ReferencesTable of contents, footnote, endnote, citations, bibliography, captions, index
MailingsEnvelopes, labels, mail merge
ReviewSpelling and grammar, thesaurus, word count, comments, Track Changes, compare, protect
ViewRead Mode, Print Layout, Web Layout, Outline, Draft, ruler, gridlines, zoom, split
  • Print settings (File, Print): Print All Pages, Print Selection, Print Current Page, and Custom Print, where you type only specific pages such as 1,3,5-7. You can also choose one-sided or both sides, collated, orientation, paper size, margins and pages per sheet.
  • Shading puts a background colour behind selected text, a paragraph or table cells. Borders draw lines around them. Text highlight colour marks text like a highlighter pen.
  • Mail merge joins one main document (a letter) with a data source (an Excel list or Outlook contacts) to make many personalised letters, envelopes, labels or emails.
  • Track Changes records every edit so another person can accept or reject it. Comments are notes in the margin.
  • Format Painter (the brush icon) copies formatting from one place to another. Double-click it to use it many times.
  • Header and footer repeat at the top and bottom of every page. A section break lets one part of the document have different margins, orientation or headers.
  • Drop cap makes the first letter of a paragraph large. Watermark is faint text such as CONFIDENTIAL behind the page.
  • AutoCorrect fixes common typing mistakes as you type. AutoText and Quick Parts store reusable text.
  • Macros record a series of steps to replay them; a Word file with macros is saved as .docm.

concepts.title: Excel basics: cells, ranges and references
concepts.body:
• A workbook holds worksheets. A worksheet is a grid of rows (numbers 1, 2, 3) and columns (letters A, B, ... Z, AA, AB ...).
  • A cell address (cell reference) is column letter plus row number. The value in column A, row 10 is referred to as A10. The selected cell is the active cell; its address shows in the Name Box.
  • A range is written with a colon: A1:A10 is ten cells. A comma joins separate ranges: SUM(A1:A3, C1) adds four cells.
  • A reference to another sheet: Sheet2!B4.
Written asTypeWhen copied
A1RelativeBoth column and row change when the formula is copied
$A$1AbsoluteNothing changes; the cell is locked
$A1MixedColumn A stays fixed; the row changes
A$1MixedRow 1 stays fixed; the column changes

Press F4 while editing a reference to cycle A1, $A$1, A$1, $A1.

Mini example: =A1*$B$1 in C1 copied down to C2 becomes =A2*$B$1. The A1 part moves one row; the $B$1 part stays.

A circular reference is a formula that refers to its own cell, for example =A1+1 typed in A1.

concepts.title: Excel formulas and functions
concepts.body:
Every formula starts with =. Operators are worked out in this order: negation (−), percent (%), power (^), multiply and divide (* /), add and subtract (+ −), join text (&), then comparisons (= < >). So =2+3*4^2 gives 2 + 3 × 16 = 50.

CategoryFunctions
Math and trigSUM, SUMIF, SUMIFS, PRODUCT, ROUND, ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN, INT, TRUNC, MOD, ABS, SQRT, POWER, PI, SIN, COS, TAN, RAND, RANDBETWEEN, CEILING, FLOOR
StatisticalAVERAGE, AVERAGEIF, COUNT, COUNTA, COUNTBLANK, COUNTIF, MAX, MIN, MEDIAN, MODE, STDEV, LARGE, SMALL, RANK
LogicalIF, AND, OR, NOT, IFERROR
TextLEN, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, UPPER, LOWER, PROPER, TRIM, CONCAT (CONCATENATE), TEXT
Date and timeTODAY, NOW, DATE, DAY, MONTH, YEAR
Lookup and referenceVLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, MATCH, INDEX

Note: SUM is listed under Math and trig, but AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX and MIN are Statistical functions.

FormulaResult or use
=COUNT(A1:A5)Counts cells that hold numbers only
=COUNTA(A1:A5)Counts all non-empty cells (numbers and text)
=COUNTBLANK(A1:A5)Counts empty cells
=COUNTIF(A1:A9,">50")Counts cells that meet one condition
=SUMIF(A1:A9,">50")Adds only the cells that meet the condition
=IF(B2>=33,"Pass","Fail")Returns one value if the test is true, another if false
=ROUND(15.678,1)15.7 (rounds to 1 decimal place)
=INT(7.9) and =INT(−3.7)7 and −4 (INT always rounds down)
=MOD(17,5)2 (the remainder)
=VLOOKUP(value, table, col_no, FALSE)Looks for the value in the first column of the table and returns the item from column col_no of that row. FALSE means exact match.
=HLOOKUP(...)Same as VLOOKUP but searches the first row
=MATCH(value, range, 0)Returns the relative position of the value in the range, not the value itself. 0 = exact match; 1 (the default) = largest value less than or equal, for ascending data; −1 = smallest value greater than or equal, for descending data.
=INDEX(range, row, col)Returns the value at that position. INDEX with MATCH is a flexible lookup.
=LEN("India")5 (number of characters)
=TODAY(), =NOW()Current date; current date and time

Mini example: if A1:A4 hold 10, 20, 30, 40, then =MATCH(30,A1:A4,0) returns 3 because 30 is the third item.

ErrorMeaning
#####Column too narrow to show the number or date
#DIV/0!Division by zero
#N/AValue not available (a lookup found nothing)
#NAME?Excel does not recognise a function or name (often a spelling error)
#REF!The formula refers to a cell that no longer exists
#VALUE!Wrong type of value, such as text in a sum like ="abc"+1
#NUM!Invalid number, such as =SQRT(−4)
#NULL!Two ranges that do not intersect

concepts.title: Excel data, charts and sheet limits
concepts.body:
LimitExcel 2007 and later (incl. 365)Excel 2003
Rows per sheet1,048,57665,536
Columns per sheet16,384 (last column XFD)256 (last column IV)
Characters in one cell32,76732,767
Column width255 characters255 characters
Characters in a formula8,1921,024
Nested function levels647
Sheet name length31 characters31 characters
  • A new workbook in Excel 2013 and later has 1 sheet; Excel 2007 and 2010 had 3. The default column width is 8.43 characters.
  • Inserting a row pushes the rows below it down; inserting a column pushes columns to the right. Formulas adjust their references automatically.
  • Sort arranges rows in order (A to Z, smallest to largest). Filter (Ctrl+Shift+L) hides rows that do not match. Freeze Panes (View tab) keeps headings visible while scrolling.
  • Conditional Formatting (Home tab) colours cells by rule. Data Validation (Data tab) limits what can be typed. Remove Duplicates and Text to Columns are on the Data tab.
  • PivotTable (Insert tab) summarises a large table. Goal Seek (Data, What-If Analysis) finds the input that gives a wanted result.
  • AutoFill: drag the fill handle (small square at the cell corner) to continue a series such as Jan, Feb, Mar or 2, 4, 6.
ChartBest for
Column or barComparing amounts across categories
LineTrend over time
PieParts of a whole; only one data series
DoughnutParts of a whole; can show more than one series
Scatter (XY)Relation between two sets of numbers
AreaSize of change over time
HistogramFrequency of values in ranges (bins)
SparklineTiny chart inside one cell

Press F11 to make a chart on a new chart sheet, or Alt+F1 to put it on the same sheet.

concepts.title: PowerPoint
concepts.body:
KeysWhat it does in PowerPoint
F5Start the slide show from the first slide
Shift+F5Start from the current slide
EscEnd the slide show
Ctrl+MInsert a new slide
Ctrl+DDuplicate the selected slide or object
N, Enter, Space, Right arrowNext slide or animation (during a show)
P, Backspace, Left arrowPrevious slide (during a show)
Number then EnterJump to that slide (during a show)
B or full stopBlack screen (during a show)
W or commaWhite screen (during a show)
Ctrl+PPen pointer (during a show); print (while editing)
  • Views: Normal (the default editing view), Outline View, Slide Sorter (thumbnails to reorder slides), Notes Page, Reading View and Slide Show. Master views: Slide Master, Handout Master and Notes Master.
  • The Slide Master controls the fonts, colours, background and placeholder positions of every slide. Change it once and all slides follow.
  • A template (.potx) is a ready-made file with a design, layouts and sometimes sample content, so a presentation looks consistent and is quick to build. A theme is a set of colours, fonts and effects.
  • Placeholders are the dotted boxes in a layout. Text typed into a loose text box instead of a placeholder does not follow the layout and can move out of place when content changes.
  • Transitions are effects between slides (Transitions tab). Animations move objects on one slide (Animations tab). The Animation Painter copies an animation.
  • Slides can be inserted, duplicated, hidden, reordered or deleted (select the slide and press Delete), so a talk can be changed without rebuilding it.
  • To make a blank presentation: File, New, Blank Presentation (or Ctrl+N).
  • Rehearse Timings records how long each slide stays up. Custom Slide Show plays only chosen slides. Speaker notes are visible to the presenter, not the audience.
  • PowerPoint tabs: File, Home, Insert, Draw, Design, Transitions, Animations, Slide Show, Record, Review, View.

concepts.title: The Office window and file types
concepts.body:
PartWhat it is
Title barTop strip showing the file name and program name
Quick Access ToolbarSmall toolbar (Save, Undo, Redo) at the top left; you can add buttons to it
RibbonBand below the title bar with tabs (Home, Insert ...). Each tab has groups of commands. Ctrl+F1 hides or shows it.
File tab (Backstage view)New, Open, Save, Save As, Print, Share, Export, Options
Dialog box launcherSmall arrow at the corner of a ribbon group that opens the full dialog
Status barBottom strip: page and word count in Word, Sum and Average of selected cells in Excel, zoom slider
Name Box and formula barExcel only: the Name Box shows the active cell address; the formula bar shows its contents or formula
Mini toolbarSmall formatting toolbar that appears when you select text
ProgramDefault (2007 and later)Old (2003)Others
Word.docx.doc.dotx (template), .docm (with macros)
Excel.xlsx.xls.xltx (template), .xlsm (with macros), .csv
PowerPoint.pptx.ppt.potx (template), .ppsx (opens straight as a show)
Access.accdb.mdb
Publisher, OneNote, Outlook.pub, .one, .pst (mail store)

Other suites: Google Docs, Sheets and Slides (online); LibreOffice Writer, Calc and Impress (free, open source); Apple Pages, Numbers and Keynote.

varieties.name: Word and common Office shortcuts
varieties.how: Learn shortcuts in families: B, I, U for style; L, E, R, J for alignment; C, X, V, Z, Y for editing; N, O, S, P, W for files. Ctrl+K is hyperlink and F12 is Save As.

example.q: Which keyboard shortcut closes the current document in MS Word but keeps Word open?
steps: Alt+F4 closes the whole program window.
Ctrl+W (or Ctrl+F4) closes only the active document.

varieties.name: Word features and menus
varieties.how: Ask what the feature produces, then match it to its tab: layout things on Layout, footnotes and contents on References, mail merge on Mailings, Track Changes on Review.

example.q: In MS Word, which print setting lets you print only pages 2, 5 and 7?
steps: Print All Pages prints everything; Print Current Page prints one page.
Custom Print lets you type a page list such as 2,5,7.

varieties.name: Excel formulas and functions
varieties.how: Work out each function on its own, then combine. Remember the order: power before multiply before add, and INT always rounds down.

steps: MOD(17,5) is the remainder of 17 ÷ 5, which is 2.

varieties.name: Excel cells and references
varieties.how: Count how many columns and rows the formula moves. Shift every part without a $ by that amount; leave every part with a $ in front unchanged.

example.q: Cell C1 contains =A1+$B$1. It is copied to D3. What formula does D3 show?
steps: C1 to D3 is 1 column right and 2 rows down.
A1 is relative, so it becomes B3.

varieties.name: Excel data, charts and sheet limits
varieties.how: Match the chart to the job (pie for parts of a whole, line for trends over time). For limits, remember 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns (XFD) from Excel 2007 onwards.

example.q: What is the last column in a worksheet of MS Excel 365?
steps: The letters run A to Z, AA to ZZ, then AAA onwards, ending at XFD.

varieties.name: Excel keyboard shortcuts
varieties.how: Excel keys differ from Word: F2 edits a cell, F4 locks references, Ctrl+; gives the date and Ctrl+Shift+; gives the time, Shift+F11 adds a sheet.

example.q: Which shortcut enters the current time in an Excel cell?
steps: Adding Shift, Ctrl+Shift+; enters the time.

varieties.name: PowerPoint slides, views and keys
varieties.how: F5 starts from the beginning, Shift+F5 from the current slide, Esc ends. Slide Master changes all slides at once; Slide Sorter is for reordering.

example.q: Which PowerPoint view shows all slides as small thumbnails so they can be rearranged easily?
steps: Normal view shows one slide for editing.
Slide Sorter view shows thumbnails of every slide for reordering.

varieties.name: Office screen and file types
varieties.how: Picture the window from top to bottom: title bar and Quick Access Toolbar, then the ribbon, then (in Excel) the Name Box and formula bar, then the work area, then the status bar.

example.q: In MS Excel, which part of the window shows the address of the active cell?
steps: The formula bar shows what is inside the cell.
The Name Box, just left of the formula bar, shows its address such as B4.

tips: Many past questions name "MS-Word 365" or "MS-Excel 365". The answers are the same as for Office 2016 to 2021.
Ctrl+E is centre in Word and PowerPoint but Flash Fill in Excel. Ctrl+D is the Font dialog in Word, Fill Down in Excel and Duplicate in PowerPoint.
F5 is Go To in Word but starts the slide show in PowerPoint. F7 is spelling in every Office program.
In Excel, ##### in a cell just means the column is too narrow.
Remember the two grid sizes as pairs: 1,048,576 by 16,384 (XFD) now, and 65,536 by 256 (IV) in Excel 2003.
MATCH returns a position, VLOOKUP returns a value. INDEX turns a position back into a value.
traps: Ctrl+Y is redo; Ctrl+Z is undo.
Ctrl+; is the date and Ctrl+Shift+; is the time, not the other way round.
COUNT counts numbers only. COUNTA also counts text. Neither counts blank cells.
Alt+F4 closes the whole program; Ctrl+W or Ctrl+F4 closes only the document.
In $A1 the column is locked; in A$1 the row is locked. The $ locks whatever comes right after it.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut makes selected text bold in MS Word?
questions.solution: Ctrl+B = Bold, Ctrl+I = Italic, Ctrl+U = Underline.

questions.q: The shortcut Ctrl+Z is used to:
questions.solution: Ctrl+Z undoes the last action. Ctrl+Y redoes it.

questions.q: In MS PowerPoint, which key starts the slide show from the first slide?
questions.solution: F5 starts the slide show from the beginning. Shift+F5 starts from the current slide.

questions.q: In MS Excel, the reference $A$1 is a(n):
questions.solution: The $ sign before both the column (A) and the row (1) locks both, so $A$1 is an absolute reference. It does not change when the formula is copied.

questions.q: In MS Word, Ctrl+J is used to:
questions.solution: Ctrl+J aligns text to both left and right margins (justify). Ctrl+E is centre and Ctrl+K inserts a hyperlink.

questions.q: Which shortcut inserts the current date in an Excel cell?
questions.solution: Ctrl+; (semicolon) enters today's date. Ctrl+Shift+; enters the current time, Ctrl+D fills down and Alt+= is AutoSum.

questions.q: In Excel, A1 = 10, A2 = 20, A3 = "abc", A4 is blank and A5 = 30. What does =COUNTA(A1:A5) return?
questions.solution: COUNTA counts every non-empty cell: A1, A2, A3 (text) and A5 = 4 cells. (=COUNT would give 3 because it counts numbers only.)

questions.q: Which shortcut starts a PowerPoint slide show from the current slide?
questions.solution: Shift+F5 starts the show from the slide you are on. F5 alone starts from slide 1.
